key.name: toggle-picker
key.summary: Open the workspace picker

key.name: open-browser
key.summary: Open or focus the browser of the current session

key.name: open-git
key.summary: Open or focus the git client for the current session

key.name: snap-presets
key.summary: Snap zone presets, each a name and a list of tiles
key.description: Tiles are fractions of the work area. Held down while dragging, the modifier key highlights the zone of the active preset under the pointer and the window is placed there on release.

key.name: snap-preset
key.summary: Index of the active preset in snap-presets

key.name: snap-modifier
key.summary: Modifier that arms snapping while dragging a window

key.name: toggle-clipboard
key.summary: Open the clipboard history

key.name: clipboard-size
key.summary: How many clipboard entries are kept

key.name: clipboard-ignore-passwords
key.summary: Skip entries marked by a password manager
key.description: Managers announce them through the x-kde-passwordManagerHint mime type. Sources that do not set it, such as browsers and terminals, are not covered by this.

key.name: search-depth
key.summary: How many directory levels below a search path are scanned
key.description: A directory holding a .git is taken as a repository and not descended into, anything else is followed until this depth.

key.name: search-exclude
key.summary: Directory names never descended into while scanning
key.description: These hold dependencies or build output and never a project of their own, so skipping them keeps deeper scans cheap.

key.name: search-paths
key.summary: Directories scanned for git repositories

key.name: home-label
key.summary: Name of the reserved workspace in the picker
key.description: Listed first so the workspace below the session range is always reachable from the picker, not only through its shortcut.

key.name: first-workspace-index
key.summary: Lowest GNOME workspace index usable for sessions, zero based
key.description: Workspaces below this index are left alone, so the first one stays reserved for personal use.

key.name: browser-command
key.summary: Browser binary used to open a workspace window

key.name: browser-desktop-id
key.summary: Desktop id used to detect whether the browser is already running

key.name: session-desktop-ids
key.summary: Applications whose windows are moved onto the session workspace
key.description: Resolved through the shell window tracker, which knows the window to application mapping already.

key.name: session-layout
key.summary: Slot per application, as a fraction of the work area
key.description: A JSON array of objects with app plus either x and y or center, and optionally width and height as fractions of the work area. Without width and height the window keeps its own size and is only moved. The flag background lowers it behind the others. Applications without an entry keep their placement, an empty array disables placement entirely.

key.name: git-desktop-id
key.summary: Application that follows the active session instead of living on a workspace

key.name: claim-window-classes
key.summary: Additional window classes claimed on top of session-desktop-ids
key.description: Fallback for windows the shell cannot map to an application. Matched case insensitively against the window class and its instance.

key.name: recent-workspaces
key.summary: Recently opened workspaces, most recent first

key.name: recent-count
key.summary: How many recent workspaces are listed while the search is empty

key.name: claim-seconds
key.summary: How long newly created windows are claimed after opening a session

key.name: editor-command
key.summary: Editor command, the project path is appended

key.name: editor-desktop-id
key.summary: Desktop id of the editor, used when restoring a stored session

key.name: session-apps
key.summary: Arrangement last seen per workspace, as JSON
key.description: Maps a workspace name to the same tile format as session-layout, capturing which applications were open and where. Written whenever the picker opens and preferred over session-layout when reopening.
